emma (devex): Heads up — my sample app deploy to Vercel Edge started failing after I updated our SDK exports map. Getting ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED when importing @redwood/inference-sdk from the edge build.

sam (eng-runtime): Can you paste the exact exports block you changed?

emma (devex): Sure, pasted from package.json in the release branch:
```json
"exports": {
  "./package.json": "./package.json",
  "./*": {
    "node": "./dist/node/*.js",
    "default": "./dist/esm/*.js"
  }
}
```

cleo (eng): That pattern (conditional + wildcard) is the usual suspect. Many edge runtimes / bundlers don't evaluate the "node" condition and will try to resolve using the default path but then fail on particular import requests. Vercel's Edge runtime needs an explicit "."/import entry for the package entrypoint.

raj (eng-platform): We built both dist/esm and dist/node outputs, but wildcard exports can cause requests like "import {createClient} from '@redwood/inference-sdk'" to not map to a concrete file. Edge bundlers sometimes don't support the "node" conditional at all.

emma (devex): Error snippet: "Error: Failed to resolve module specifier '@redwood/inference-sdk'. ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED" and then the deploy logs show a fallback attempt that throws "SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module" when it hits a CJS file.

sam (eng-runtime): Quick fix that worked for me locally — add an explicit package entry with import/require and a top-level dot mapping:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/node/index.cjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
That makes the import resolution deterministic for edge bundlers.

cleo (eng): Also check package.json's "types" and "type" fields. Consumers using TS or bundlers expect "types": "dist/esm/index.d.ts" and sometimes "type": "module" in the ESM build. Missing or mismatched types can confuse some toolchains.

emma (devex): I tried the explicit "." mapping and the Vercel deploy succeeded. Can submit a patch.

raj (eng-platform): Can we add a small CI smoke test? e.g., a tiny sample that imports the package and we run esbuild rollup with format=esm and also run node ESM require compatibility. Catch this before releasing.

sam (eng-runtime): Good idea — script to run: `esbuild sample/index.ts --bundle --format=esm --target=esnext` and a simple node test `node --input-type=module -e "import('@redwood/inference-sdk').then(console.log)"` should fail fast.

cleo (eng): Note for future: avoid over-relying on Node-only condition keys. Use explicit conditions: import/require/browser/worker/default and a clear "." entry to ensure bundlers and edge runtimes resolve correctly. Document expected package layout in SDK contributing guide.

emma (devex): Opening PR 2384 with the exports fix, types update, and a sample-app CI smoke test. Will add a changelog note and link to the reasoning. Sorry for the churn — caught before wider rollout :thumbsup:

buildbot: CI: release/2026.03.20 — 1 failing job: sample-app-exports-compat. Full logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/1234

raj (eng-platform): I'll hold the release promotion until PR merges. Thanks everyone for quick triage.
